name: Libya
tagline: Leptis Magna, and the sand sea behind it
summary: The best-preserved Roman city on the Mediterranean, Greek Cyrene on its escarpment, and the Ubari lakes in a sand sea — a country whose archaeology is world-class and whose access is not simple.
when: Late autumn to early spring. Check what your government says before you plan anything.

entries.caption: Leptis Magna
entries.description: A Roman city of a hundred thousand people, buried by sand and dug out almost complete.
entries.subject: the colonnaded forum and basilica of Leptis Magna

entries.caption: The Sand Sea and the Jebel
entries.description: The Ubari sand sea in the southwest, and the green Jebel Akhdar behind Benghazi.
entries.subject: dunes of the Ubari sand sea with a palm-fringed lake below

entries.caption: Desert Survivors
entries.description: Barbary sheep in the Acacus, dorcas gazelle on the gravel plains, and very little else.
entries.subject: a Barbary sheep on rock in the Acacus mountains

entries.caption: Tracking, Not Driving
entries.description: The wildlife is thin and shy. What you go out to see is the country it survives in.
entries.subject: a desert track crossing gravel plain in the Libyan Sahara

entries.caption: The Acacus
entries.description: Volcanic rock arches and towers on the Algerian border, with rock art under them.
entries.subject: a natural rock arch in the Acacus mountains at sunset

entries.caption: Wadi Country
entries.description: No permanent rivers. The water is in wadis that run once a decade and in springs at the oases.
entries.subject: a spring-fed pool among palms in a Libyan desert oasis

entries.caption: The Ubari Lakes
entries.description: Salt lakes between dunes, the last of them dense enough to float in.
entries.subject: Gaberoun lake between high dunes in the Ubari sand sea

entries.caption: Two Thousand Kilometres of Coast
entries.description: The longest Mediterranean coastline of any African country, and almost none of it built on.
entries.subject: an empty white sand beach on the Libyan Mediterranean coast

entries.caption: The Green Mountain
entries.description: Juniper and cypress on the Jebel Akhdar, the only real forest in the country.
entries.subject: juniper forest on the slopes of the Jebel Akhdar

entries.caption: Into the Acacus
entries.description: Four-wheel-drive expeditions of a week, camping under the arches with Tuareg guides.
entries.subject: a desert camp under a rock arch in the Acacus at night

entries.caption: Arab, Berber, Tuareg, Tebu
entries.description: Four peoples and three languages, and a coast that has been Phoenician, Greek, Roman, Ottoman and Italian.
entries.subject: a busy market street in the medina of Tripoli

entries.caption: The Tuareg and the Tebu
entries.description: The Tuareg in the southwest around Ghat, the Tebu in the Tibesti foothills in the southeast.
entries.subject: a Tebu man beside a camel in southern Libya

entries.caption: Bazin and Bsisa
entries.description: Bazin with lamb and paprika, couscous on Fridays, and shorba on the table all Ramadan.
entries.subject: a shared plate of Libyan bazin with lamb and sauce

entries.caption: Ghat and the Desert Festivals
entries.description: The Ghat festival brings Tuareg from three countries for racing, music and poetry.
entries.subject: Tuareg riders racing camels at the Ghat festival

entries.caption: Silver and Leather
entries.description: Tuareg silver crosses, tooled leather from Ghadames, and Berber weaving in the Nafusa.
entries.subject: a Tuareg silver cross pendant on tooled leather

entries.caption: Cyrene and Sabratha
entries.description: A Greek city on an escarpment above the sea, and a Roman theatre facing the water at Sabratha.
entries.subject: the three-storey Roman theatre at Sabratha facing the sea

entries.caption: Five Sites, All of Them Major
entries.description: Leptis, Sabratha, Cyrene, Ghadames and the Acacus rock art — every one on the World Heritage list.
entries.subject: prehistoric rock engravings of giraffe in the Acacus

entries.caption: Tripoli and Benghazi
entries.description: An Ottoman medina inside Italian arcades in Tripoli, and Benghazi rebuilding.
entries.subject: the Ottoman medina and clock tower of Tripoli

entries.caption: Ghadames
entries.description: A covered mud-brick town where the streets are tunnels and the roofs are the women's road.
entries.subject: the whitewashed roof terraces and covered alleys of Ghadames

entries.caption: Tea, Three Times
entries.description: Poured from a height, three glasses, and no conversation is finished before the third.
entries.subject: hands pouring Libyan tea from a height into small glasses

entries.caption: Roman Cities Are Good for This
entries.description: Leptis is enormous, empty and safe to run around in, which not every ruin is.
entries.subject: children running along a Roman street at Leptis Magna

entries.caption: The Jebel Akhdar
entries.description: Walking on the green mountain between Greek tombs cut into the rock.
entries.subject: a walking path past rock-cut Greek tombs on the Jebel Akhdar

entries.caption: Thin on the Ground
entries.description: There is very little at the top end here, and what exists is in Tripoli.
entries.subject: a restored merchant's courtyard house in Tripoli medina

entries.caption: What the Desert Keeps
entries.description: Sand buried Leptis Magna for a thousand years, which is why there is so much of it left.
entries.subject: sand drifted against the standing columns of a Roman street

entries.caption: Stone and Sea
entries.description: Sabratha's theatre with the Mediterranean through its arches, in the last hour of light.
entries.subject: the arches of Sabratha's theatre with the sea beyond at sunset

entries.caption: Waw an Namus
entries.description: A black volcanic caldera in the middle of the Sahara with green lakes at the bottom.
entries.subject: the black volcanic crater and green lakes of Waw an Namus

entries.caption: Why Libya
entries.description: Because Leptis Magna is the best Roman city left anywhere, and hardly anyone has stood in it.
entries.subject: a single visitor in the vast forum of Leptis Magna
